name: Zacchaeus
whenBasis: Jesus' ministry, from the fifteenth year of Tiberius (Luke 3:1), AD 28–29, to the crucifixion under Pilate, usually dated AD 30 or 33.
summary: A chief tax collector at Jericho, very wealthy, who wanted to see Jesus but was too short to see over the crowd, so he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree. Jesus stopped, looked up and said, “Zacchaeus, hurry down, for I must stay at your house today.” The crowd grumbled that he had gone to be the guest of a sinner. Zacchaeus stood and promised half his possessions to the poor and fourfold repayment to anyone he had cheated.
body: Jesus answers, “Today salvation has come to this house, because this man too is a son of Abraham. For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.”

later.text: The Apostolic Constitutions (≈AD 380) name Zacchaeus the tax collector as the first bishop of Caesarea.
